member.name: T:SysWeaver.Net.ApiHttpEntry
member.summary: A web API end point: an HTTP request handler bound to a single method on a service instance. Created through , normally by for every [WebApi] method it discovers.
member.remarks: The method may take zero or one argument, optionally followed by a trailing context parameter, and may return void, a value, / or /. A strongly typed invoker is compiled (via expression trees) for GET and POST at creation time. GET reads the argument from the query string using , POST reads it from the request body (decompressed according to Content-Encoding and deserialized according to Content-Type). Results are serialized according to the Accept header, unless the method is marked with and returns of bytes. Authorization, rate limiting and caching are not performed by this class: uses , , , and before invoking it. Instances are immutable after creation and thread safe.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.Net.ApiHttpServerModule
member.summary: The Web API engine: an that exposes public instance methods marked with as HTTP end points (one per method).
member.remarks: URLs are composed as [Root]/[root argument]/[type WebApiUrl]/[method url or name] (see ). Typically created and populated by the API micro service, which calls for every local service instance and wires implementations to the audit events. Lookups are lock-free; adding is serialized internally, so registration is thread safe. Only the exact URL is matched (no prefix matching) and requests using are ignored.

member.summary: A reference counted template match pattern (compiled to a regular expression).

member.name: M:SysWeaver.Net.HttpServerBase.AddTemplateMatch(System.String)
member.summary: Add a template match pattern (reference counted, adding the same pattern again increments the count). If a local url matches a template pattern, variable substitution ("${Name}") will be performed within the data (must be UTF-8 text). Patterns can use wildcards '*' (matches zero or more chars) or '?' (matches one). If the pattern starts with '$' the rest of the pattern is a regular expression. If the pattern starts with '#' the match should be case insensitive. If the pattern starts with '$#' the rest of the pattern is a regular expression matched case insensitive.
member.param: The pattern
member.remarks: Whether a url is a template is cached per local url the first time it's requested, so adding a pattern doesn't affect urls that have already been served. Query string parameters are available as variables in templates and take precedence over all other variables (see ).

member.name: M:SysWeaver.Net.HttpServerBase.RemoveTemplateMatch(System.String)
member.summary: Remove a previously added template match pattern (decrements the reference count, removed when it reaches zero).
member.param: The pattern

Not used
True to create a template state even if no pattern matches (language templates)

member.name: M:SysWeaver.Net.HttpServerBase.GetVars(System.Boolean,SysWeaver.Net.HttpServerRequest)
member.summary: Get the per request template variables. If is true, "Server.UTC", "Request.Prefix", "Request.IP", "Session.Lang" and (if a user is logged in) "Session.User", "Session.UserName", "Session.Email", "Session.Domain" and "Session.NickName" are added. Query string parameters are never used as template variables.
member.param: True to include the dynamic variables

member.remarks: These variables take precedence over static variables and variable groups when a template is applied. Values are inserted as is unless the template uses an encoding modifier. "Server.UTC" is formatted as "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss" (24 hour clock, invariant culture).

member.name: M:SysWeaver.Net.HttpServerBase.GetTranslationVars(System.String,SysWeaver.LanguageTemplate)
member.summary: Get the translations of a language template as variables (untranslated if there is no translator or the language is English). The result only depends on the language and is cached in , so variables inside of the translations are NOT substituted here, that is done per request by (else the values of the first request would be cached and shown to everyone). If a translation variable whose name starts with 'V' is only inserted html encoded in the template (ex: "${#Vr1}"), html encoding transforms of its inner variables are removed (ex: "Welcome ${#Session.NickName}" becomes "Welcome ${Session.NickName}"), so that the values aren't html encoded twice.

The language template
member.returns: The translation variables, null if the template has no texts

member.summary: An optional array of patterns for files that should be used as text templates (in addition to the built-in ones, ex: "index.html"). These files must contain text stored as UTF-8. Patterns can use wildcards '*' (matches zero or more) or '?' (matches one). If the pattern starts with '$' the rest of the pattern is a regular expression. If the pattern starts with '#' the match should be case insensitive. If the pattern starts with '$#' the rest of the pattern is a regular expression matched case insensitive.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.Net.HttpServerHosts
member.summary: Resolves the host of a request url (called for every request). A server typically has a few hosts (1 to 3), so these are kept in a small array that is searched linearly (no hashing, no allocations).
member.remarks: Also url decodes the whole url (path and query, see ) and inserts "index.html" for directory requests. The decoding happens after any normalization done by the listener, so the resulting local url may contain "../" segments (from "%2F" / "%2E") and "?" chars (from "%3F"). Thread safe, new hosts are added under a lock (copy on write lookup array). Hosts are never removed, a new is kept for every distinct "scheme://host:port" that matches a listener prefix, up to hosts. Further hosts (the Host header is client controlled) are resolved on every request without being cached, so that random Host headers can't grow the memory without bound.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.Net.IHttpRequestHandler
member.summary: Produces the response for a request, returned by an . The properties describe how the server should treat the response (auth, client and server caching, compression, templates, transformers, rate limiting), the server performs those steps and calls or to get the actual data.
member.remarks: Handlers are frequently cached and shared between concurrent requests, so implementations must be thread safe and should not store per request state (the exception being , which is only set on per request handler instances). Order of calls: is checked, then is called (304 handling), then (if server caching is enabled) and finally Get or GetAsync on a cache miss.

member.name: P:SysWeaver.Net.IHttpRequestHandler.Name
member.summary: The name of this request handler (defaults to the type name), used for performance tracking.

member.name: P:SysWeaver.Net.IHttpRequestHandler.Redirected
member.summary: If non-null, the server processes this request instead of the incoming one (and disposes it if it's ). Used internally when a request is redirected/rewritten, implementations should only store the value.

member.name: P:SysWeaver.Net.IHttpRequestHandler.ClientCacheDuration
member.summary: The duration in seconds that the client should keep the response cached (basically setting up the Cache-Control header in the response).

member.name: P:SysWeaver.Net.IHttpRequestHandler.RequestCacheDuration
member.summary: The duration in seconds that the same request should be cached on the server, i.e Get / GetAsync for the same request from multiple clients within this period will only result in a single call to these methods (reduces server load). Zero disables server side caching. If negative, the per session cache is used with the absolute value as duration (else a global cache is used).
member.remarks: The cache key is built from (or the url), the request type, the Accept-Encoding header, the http method and (for localized content) the language. Responses that differ per user must use a negative duration or a user specific cache key.

member.name: P:SysWeaver.Net.IHttpRequestHandler.IsLocalized
member.summary: If true, the response is localized (language dependent) and the session language is made part of the server cache key.

member.name: P:SysWeaver.Net.IHttpRequestHandler.Compression

member.name: P:SysWeaver.Net.IHttpRequestHandler.Decoder
member.summary: If the data returned by Get / GetAsync is pre-compressed, the decoder of that compression format, else null. The server sends the data as is if the client accepts the encoding, else it decompresses (and possibly re-compresses) it.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.Net.RedirectHttpServerModule
member.summary: A http module that redirects requests whose full url starts with a configured prefix (ex: http to https upgrades), and that serves the "external info" redirects (country, currency, user agent, ip and mac lookups on external sites).
member.remarks: Redirections come from or from a monitored text file (). If no redirections are configured (and no file is used), is used. A '*' in a redirection is replaced with the bare host name of the request (ex: "example.com") and default ports are removed (request urls never contain them), the resolved redirections are cached per host. The redirect response is written directly (), so no auth checks are made.

member.name: M:SysWeaver.Net.RedirectHttpServerModule.Handler(SysWeaver.Net.HttpServerRequest)
member.summary: If the request url starts with a configured prefix, writes a redirect response (the matched prefix is replaced, the rest of the url is kept).
member.param: The request
member.returns: if a redirect was written, else null
member.remarks: A '*' in a redirection is replaced with the bare host name of the request (ex: "example.com"), and default ports (":80" for http, ":443" for https) are removed from the resolved redirections, since request urls never contain them (ex: "http://*:80/" matches "http://example.com/"). The prefix is matched against the decoded request url (), but the remainder is taken from the undecoded url (), so percent encoded chars (ex: "%3F", "%23", "%25", "%20", "%0D%0A") keep their encoding (no changed meaning, no header injection). If the raw url is the decoded url (ex: ), or the prefix can't be mapped to the raw url, the remainder is taken from the decoded url. Chars that are invalid in an url or in a header (controls, space, non-ASCII etc) are always percent encoded. The "index.html" inserted by the server for directory requests () is not included in the remainder.

member.name: F:SysWeaver.Net.RedirectHttpServerModuleParams.Redirections
member.summary: The redirections to make (ignored if is set). Invalid entries are ignored with a warning. If empty, an http to https redirection is used ().

member.name: F:SysWeaver.Net.RedirectHttpServerModuleParams.Filename
member.summary: If this is non-empty redirection entries are read from this file. Filename can contain environment variables. The file is monitored for any updates and reloaded when changed (if the file contains any invalid row, the previous redirections are kept). The file must be a UTF8 encoded text file, where each non-empty row not starting with a # is a redirection (text after a # is a comment). The format of a row is "From To [Code]" (Code defaults to 302, valid codes are 301, 302, 307 and 308), example: http://*:80/ https://*:443/ 302 Quotes may be used, example: "http://*:80/" "https://*:443/"

member.summary: A http module that serves static content registered at runtime (embedded resources, memory, text or streams), keyed on the exact local url (GET requests only).
member.remarks: Typically used to serve the embedded web assets of all loaded assemblies. member.name: T:SysWeaver.HttpTransformer.CachedTransformer
member.summary: Base class for transformer services that convert served files (by mime type or file extension) into alternative, typically smaller, variants (pre-compressed, re-encoded images etc) that are cached on disc and selected per request.
member.remarks: Derived classes register handlers using . The server invokes handlers for matching files; an in-memory cache (1 hour) keyed by local url and etag maps to a ; misses are validated against disc and otherwise built (in the background or directly, see ). Files are named by a 26 character hash of the key, distributed over the data folders, and pruned when not accessed for days (one folder is scanned every 15 minutes). Thread safe.

member.name: T:SysWeaver.Security.LinuxFirewallHandler
member.summary: A firewall handler for Linux, supporting the three most common firewalls: ufw (Ubuntu / Debian), firewalld (RHEL, Fedora, CentOS, SUSE) and plain nftables. The firewall that is active is detected (see ), rules are only added to that firewall.

remarks.para: All changes (and most status queries) require root, a process that isn't root gets a warning and false (like without elevation), "sudo" is never used. If no firewall is active, nothing blocks the port: and return true (with an info / debug message).
All programs are started directly (no shell) with every value passed as a separate argument. Rule names are sanitized (see ) by both and , only names that are empty after sanitizing are refused.
Rules that weren't added by this handler (other names / comments) are never changed or removed.
How rules are identified and stored:

list.item: ufw: a rule with the rule name as comment, ex: "ufw allow in proto tcp from any to any port 443 comment 'name'" (IPv4 and IPv6 if enabled in ufw), permanent. Outbound rules allow traffic from the local port: "ufw allow out proto tcp from any port 443 to any". Existing rules are found by parsing the "### tuple ###" lines of "/etc/ufw/user.rules" and "/etc/ufw/user6.rules" and deleted by their exact rule spec. If an identical rule without (or with another) comment exists, it satisfies the rule: nothing is added for that address family (ufw would otherwise take over that rule and change its comment, so that a later would delete it), an info message is logged.

firewalld: a SysWeaver owned service (see , its short description is the rule name) with the port(s), added to the default zone, permanent and runtime. Creating or changing the service runs "firewall-cmd --reload" (that also discards runtime only changes made by others), validating an existing valid service doesn't. Ports opened by others (zone ports or other services) are left alone, the own service is added anyway. firewalld zones don't filter outgoing traffic, so an outbound rule isn't needed (true is returned without any change).

nftables: a rule like "tcp dport 443 accept comment \"name\"" is inserted first in every native filter base chain hooked to input (or output for outbound, "tcp sport 443"), in the families inet, ip and ip6 (tables named "firewalld" and the iptables-nft tables, with chains named INPUT / OUTPUT etc, are skipped). The rules are added to the existing chains (an accept in a separate table wouldn't override a drop in another table, since every base chain must accept a packet). The rules are runtime only (not saved to "/etc/nftables.conf"), they are lost on reboot or when the ruleset is reloaded (the http servers add them on every start). If no such chain exists, nothing filters the traffic and nothing is added.

remarks.para: Not supported: iptables only systems (iptables-legacy, or iptables rules without ufw / firewalld), those are reported as "no firewall".

member.summary: Map some letters without a Unicode decomposition to ASCII.

member.name: M:SysWeaver.Security.LinuxFirewallHandler.SanitizeRuleName(System.String)
member.summary:
Make a valid rule name (see ) from any string, deterministically: the same input always gives the same name, so finds a rule added by (both use this method). A valid name is returned unchanged.
Diacritics are removed (Unicode decomposition, ex: "ä" gives "a") and some letters are transliterated (ex: "ß" gives "ss", "ø" gives "o").
Any other char that isn't allowed is replaced by '_', a run of replaced chars gives a single '_' (ex: "a\"'b" gives "a_b").
Leading and trailing spaces are removed.
If the result is longer than , it's truncated and '_' + an 8 hex digit FNV-1a hash (of the UTF-8 input) is appended.
member.param: The rule name, may be null
member.returns: The sanitized name, or null if nothing is left (null, empty or only spaces)

member.name: M:SysWeaver.Security.LinuxFirewallHandler.GetFirewalldServiceName(System.String)
member.summary: Get the name of the firewalld service that is used for a rule name: + the lower case name (other chars than a-z and 0-9 replaced by '-', at most 32 chars) + '-' + a 32 bit FNV-1a hash (8 hex digits) of the exact rule name (UTF-8). Ex: "SysWeaver MyApp 443" gives "sysweaver-sysweaver-myapp-443-xxxxxxxx".
member.param: The rule name
member.returns: The service name
member.exception: is null

member.name: M:SysWeaver.Security.LinuxFirewallHandler.Detect(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Detect what firewalls are installed, enabled and active, and which one is used. The result is cached for .
member.param: True to ignore any cached result (and cache the new one)
member.returns: The detection result, never null
member.remarks:
Detection (in priority order, the first active firewall is used):
firewalld: "firewall-cmd" found, active if "firewall-cmd --state" prints "running" ("not running" or no system D-Bus: inactive, if not authorized: "systemctl is-active firewalld", unknown without systemd). Enabled: "systemctl is-enabled firewalld".
ufw: "ufw" found, active if "ufw status" prints "Status: active" (root only, else unknown). Enabled: "ENABLED=yes" in .
nftables: "nft" found, as root: active if the ruleset ("nft -j list ruleset") has a native filter base chain hooked to input or output (not firewalld's or iptables-nft's), not root: "systemctl is-active nftables" (unknown without systemd). Enabled: "systemctl is-enabled nftables".
Programs are searched in the PATH and then in the usual sbin / bin folders.
